newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-KALLIS RESCUES SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KALLIS RESCUES SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Jacques Kallis rescued South Africa with a score of 82 to help his country reach 221 for eight in 50 overs after Australia's Adam Dale had taken three quick wickets in the second of seven one-day internationals at St. George's Park on Monday.

Australian captain Mark Taylor, whose team were beaten in the first match of the series in East London on Saturday, had no hesitation in putting the hosts in to bat on a green wicket under overcast skies and 28-year-old Queensland fast bowler Dale quickly reduced South Africa to 16 for three in eight overs.
Dale had local debutant Louis Koen caught at second slip for a duck, Adam Bacher caught at mid-off for three and then bowled Daryll Cullinan for another duck.

But Kallis and the dependable Jonty Rhodes added 104 for the fourth wicket to rescue the innings with Rhodes scampering quick singles and Kallis launching Shane Warne for a towering six over square leg.
Rhodes drove a tame catch to mid-on to depart for 57 from 86 balls with seven fours but Kallis and Hansie Cronje (31) added a further 61 for the fifth wicket to continue the recovery.
Cronje and Kallis were both bowled by Jason Gillespie in the 45th over with Kallis making his fifth half-century in his 20th match. His 82 came from 118 balls with five fours and the six.
Strangely, Dale was not brought back into the attack after his first seven overs, which included three maidens and earned him three wickets for just 18 runs.

The game started inauspiciously for Australia when the two teams lined up for the playing of the respective national anthems. While South Africa enjoyed Nkosi Sikele i'Africa, the tourists had to endure Waltzing Matilda and not Advance Australia Fair after a mix-up in tapes.
